summary: The lecture covers Indian prehistory from Paleolithic to Neolithic periods and the Indus Valley Civilization, including key discoveries, major sites, urban planning, economy, script, weights, religion, and decline theories.
points: Paleolithic age in India: 2 million years ago to 10,000 BC; Robert Bruce Foote discovered first tool (1863).
Neolithic age: polished stone tools, domestication, food production; Mehrgarh earliest (7000 BC).
Indus Valley Civilization mature phase: 2600–1900 BC; first noted by Charles Masson (1826).
John Marshall announced discovery (1924); major sites: Harappa, Mohenjo-daro, Dholavira, Lothal, Kalibangan, Rakhigarhi, Banawali, Surkotada.
Urban features: grid pattern, drainage, citadel, great bath, granaries, standardized bricks (4:2:1).
Lothal: port city with dockyard; evidence of double cropping (wheat, barley).
Script: undeciphered, 400–500 signs, boustrophedon; seals show unicorn, humped bull.
Weights: binary system (1,2,4,8,16…), 16:1 ratio; linear measure 1.63 cm (Indus inch).
Religion: nature worship, mother goddess, proto-Shiva (Pashupati seal), no temples found.
Decline theories: climate change, river shifts, Aryan invasion/migration, ecological degradation.
